k_takeaway_2000_SH: At Mauna Loa, the model produces 315 ppm in 1958, rising to 423 ppm in 2024; the measured value is about 425 ppm. The model's inputs are emissions, global temperature, sea-surface temperature, an index of El Niño and La Niña (ENSO), volcanic aerosol light diffusion and nitrogen deposition, and its calibration data include the CO2 level and seasonal cycle at both Mauna Loa and the South Pole. But it is not an abstract regression: with a couple exceptions, it is designed around parameters that represent physical processes.
